# rig-service

**One shared rigctld for the station's rig, as a systemd user service**

- **Version recorded:** 1.0
- **Categories:** `rig-control`
- **Upstream:** <https://hamlib.github.io/>
- **Needs first:** `libhamlib-utils`

## What it does

Runs one hamlib `rigctld` for the operator, a systemd *user* service bound to 127.0.0.1:4532, carrying the station's radio. Every program that speaks hamlib's NET rigctl — WSJT-X, fldigi, JS8Call, Pat, gpredict and the rest — points at that one port instead of each opening the serial port itself. For a radio with no CAT it runs hamlib's dummy model keying an RTS or DTR line, so those programs are configured for it exactly as for a CAT rig.

## Why you would want it

One program owns the serial port; every other program shares it. Two programs opening the port directly is the classic digital-modes failure, and its symptom is erratic behaviour rather than an error. This settles it once: say which radio is on the station with `hammunition station set --rig`, and the service is there at every login.

## Before it will work

The station's rig values (`hammunition station set --rig …`). Membership of `dialout`, which the rig hardware class adds — log out completely afterwards, because a group added mid-session does not reach the user manager. With the rig values unset the service is deferred and the rest of an install proceeds (D-035).

- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.

## How it installs

## Known problems

Loopback is not per-user: any local account and any local process can connect to 127.0.0.1:4532 and key the transmitter, and `rigctld` has no password (its `-A` option is "not implemented"). On a single-operator laptop that is the operator's own software; on a shared machine it is a transmitter anyone logged in can key. Two operators logged in at once would each try to start a rigctld on 4532 and the second fails to bind — the station is one operator's. Changing a rig value reaches the service only through a reinstall of this unit, which `station set` prints when it changes one. Not yet run against a real radio: the service at login, the UV-50PRO's keying line and start-up keying, `--unattended` across a logout, and the loopback filter with real clients are the bench's (D-073); docs/guides/rig-control.md says what was measured.
